A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BID research, with readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-C. Material can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original diagnostic simulations, seven manipulation-task evaluations, ablations, and two real-world robot experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and real-world results and reports revised simulation comparisons and expanded analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the backward-coherence and forward-contrast losses retain the same procedure. v2 emphasizes the early-checkpoint weak policy already described in v1. Its positive-only UMI implementation is newly disclosed for the retained experiment; an underlying algorithm change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the one-dimensional diagnostic, Push-T, five RoboMimic tasks, Franka Kitchen, and two real-world tasks. Stochastic-noise and static/dynamic-target scenarios already appear in v1. Expanding analyses across these retained tasks introduces no new task coverage.

E2.justification: Lowvar, evaluated in v1 Section 5.2 and Table 1, is removed from v2 Section 5.2.1 and Figure 6. Vanilla, Warmstart, and EMA remain. The VQ-BeT and real-world comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The reported diffusion setup changes from best public checkpoints to models trained for 100-1000 epochs; weak-policy training changes from 50-100 to 10-100 epochs. Defaults change from N=30, K=10, rho=0.9, lambda=0.75 to 16, 3, 0.5, 0.5. Scaling uses a different sample-size grid and seven-task relative gains instead of Push-T scores; the revised ablation reports aggregate success rates.

E4.justification: Scalability, compatibility, and forward-contrast ablations expand from Push-T alone to all seven simulation tasks, substantially broadening evidence for these properties. Appendix A.3 now explicitly describes open-loop ablations. The horizon/context analysis, EMA sensitivity analysis, and existing stochastic-robustness studies remain.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports three random seeds for the main diffusion comparison, scalability/compatibility analyses, and forward-contrast ablation, with error bars in Figures 6, 7, and 12. v1 provides no corresponding seed counts or error bars. Existing five-checkpoint averaging in Appendix A.2 remains. The new error-bar statistic is unspecified.

E6.justification: The main diffusion results are replaced: BID exceeds EMA on Can and Kitchen in v1 Table 1, whereas EMA's plotted means slightly exceed BID's in v2 Figure 6. Reported relative improvement changes from over 26% to about 32%, with 46% reported for EMA+BID. Scaling and ablation results also change. These involve revised settings, not demonstrated same-setting gains. Diagnostic, VQ-BeT, and real-world results are retained.

T1.justification: The assumptions, consistency-reactivity inequalities, corollaries, formal definitions, and proofs in Appendix C are retained. Equation renumbering, corrected section references, and explanatory rewording do not change the mathematical content.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the action-chunking analysis and BID inference algorithm. The introduction updates the headline relative-performance claim from more than 26% to more than 32%, while retaining the same policy and task scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly explains how backward coherence alone can perpetuate a suboptimal prior plan and distinguishes low-likelihood samples from model-expert mismatch when motivating forward contrast. The computational-cost and short-context limitations, including the appendix discussions of theoretical assumptions, remain.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 reports released implementations for both policy families and supplies two repository addresses in a reproducibility statement. It also specifies temporally correlated, action-scaled Gaussian noise and discloses that dynamic picking omitted negative samples because no early UMI checkpoint was available. These materially expand reproducibility information; repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes the first-low-level-decoding claim, acknowledges concurrent value-guided work by Nakamoto et al. and IDQL, and distinguishes BID through its lack of a separate value function. References to lookahead decoding, locally typical sampling, and self-consistency are added; Holtzman et al. (2020) and Mirostat are removed. The broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and method motivation receive extensive rewriting. Simulation experiments are consolidated into nested subsections, detailed real-world descriptions move to Appendix B.2, and a reproducibility statement is added. Citation style and headings also change throughout.

P2.justification: The main numerical comparison table becomes a seven-panel bar chart. Scaling and ablation plots change axes, aggregation, displayed bars, and uncertainty displays. Real-world demonstration Figures 7-8 move to Appendix B as Figures 14-15. Typography, running headers, and figure placement are revised throughout.

improvement.justification: Suite-wide ablation and scalability analyses, three-seed reporting, and clearer implementation disclosures improve empirical support and transparency over v1. The revised method explanation and more qualified research positioning also help. These gains are tempered by removing Lowvar and the exact simulation-score table, while leaving the new error bars undefined, supporting a limited net improvement.
